key_insight: ProofCouncil shows that an author-critic LLM agent can substantially improve performance on open mathematical problems by aligning generation with review and refinement workflows used in real research.
engineering_relevance: The work is relevant for building agentic scientific assistants that combine proposal, critique, and iteration to produce more reliable reasoning on hard technical tasks.
method: Uses an author-critic architecture for mathematical problem solving
Applied to the FirstProof benchmark and to researcher-provided open problems
Releases an open-source agent-building library for reproducing and extending the system
evidence_signal: On FirstProof, 6 of 10 problems were judged correct up to minor revisions; on 30 researcher-collected open problems, 5 of 21 reviewed solutions were fully correct and 2 more were promising pending verification.
watch_item: Results depend on human referee judgment and are still limited by the difficulty of verifying open mathematical claims, so apparent progress may not always translate into fully rigorous proofs.
paper_title: ProofCouncil: An LLM Agent for Solving Open Mathematical Problems
